final_answer: Hypothesis: There is a statistically significant difference in degree completion rates between males and females in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset. The context of this hypothesis is the relationship between gender and educational attainment, as measured by the highest grade completed by the respondent in 1979. The variables chosen are "Sex of respondent, 1979" (gender) and "Highest grade completed, 1979" (degree completion rates). The t-test results show a statistically significant difference in degree completion rates between genders, with a t-statistic of -5.69 and a p-value of approximately 1.29e-08, which is much less than 0.05. This indicates that there is a significant difference in degree completion rates between males and females in the dataset.
